hiring_bar_summary.text: Two-gate bar, and the second gate is distinctive: technical competence (coding + systems design) AND a dedicated core-values interview run by trained employees from outside the hiring team. Values are not a vibe check appended to the loop - candidates report them as a separate pass/fail-style conversation.

screening_signals.claim: Four published core values are the explicit culture screen: Champion the Mission, Be a Host, Embrace the Adventure, Be a Cereal Entrepreneur
New-grad role prefers candidates able to commute to SF or Seattle offices three days per week - a location screen stated in the posting

Recruiting-integrity note in official postings: real recruiters only use @airbnb.com / @ext.airbnb.com and never ask for SSN, bank details or payment during interviews - a scam screen candidates should know

stages: Technical screen (live coding; running code required, per prep-guide reports)
Onsite/virtual loop: coding rounds, system design (low- and high-level), project deep-dive
Core-values interview(s) with interviewers outside the hiring team

basis.claim: Airbnb's careers site describes a rigorous process with values assessment; round detail is from third-party prep guides and candidate reports - labeled reported norm, not official stage list

hiring_cadence.note: New-grad SWE appears as a discrete posted role rather than a published annual cohort calendar; no official application-window dates were published in the sources fetched. Re-check the careers page each cycle.

red_flags: Values interview is a real gate: a technically strong candidate with generic 'belong anywhere' answers and no specific hosting/community stories is at risk - prep specific stories.
Level/location mismatch: corporate remote policy is broad, but the new-grad role prefers SF/Seattle hybrid - read the specific posting, not the policy page.
Impersonation scams are common enough that Airbnb postings carry an explicit warning - verify recruiter domains.
thesis_text: Bottom line: Airbnb is one of the few large tech employers where the culture interview is a structural gate, not a formality - you must pass coding/design AND a values loop judged against four published values by people outside your future team. Who gets in: no public cohort data exists, so no school or feeder percentages can be honestly quoted; the verifiable screens are CS fundamentals plus product evidence for new grads (a distinct posted role, SF/Seattle hybrid) and 10+ years with launched consumer products at Staff. Stated vs revealed: the company states belonging and anywhere-work; the new-grad posting reveals an office-anchored start (three days a week, SF/Seattle preferred) - plan for the posting, not the slogan. Routes in, ranked: (1) SWE internship -> conversion, with a lighter reported loop; (2) direct new-grad application with a strong project portfolio and values stories; (3) experienced lateral into consumer product/platform teams. Gap to close: a project deep-dive story you can defend for an hour, and two or three specific stories that map to Be a Host / Cereal Entrepreneur without sounding scripted. Plan: 30 days - build the values-story bank and one portfolio project; semester - apply to the intern/new-grad postings the moment they appear and line up a referral; year - if you miss, take a consumer-product SWE role elsewhere and lateral in at mid level. Coffee chats: recent new-grad hires and a core-values interviewer if reachable; ask how values answers are actually scored. Risks/alternatives: small new-grad intake relative to applicant volume (unquantified publicly - do not quote a rate); adjacent consumer marketplaces reward the same profile. Offer to execute: posting alerts, resume tailoring to the deep-dive, outreach list build.

known_biases_of_data: Public postings describe the roles a company is currently trying to fill, not the people it actually hired; interview-prep and review sites are self-selected candidate reports; no licensed population dataset (PDL/Coresignal-class) was available for this record, so no school/employer/major shares are stated. Airbnb-specific: the new-grad posting snapshot is months old and the role may have closed/reopened; Glassdoor intern sample is small and self-selected.
